verses.zh: （亚萨的诗。）大能者　神―耶和华已经发言招呼天下，从日出之地到日落之处。
verses.en: A psalm by Asaph.El, God, the Lord[NOTE:1] has spoken,and summoned the earth to come from the east and west.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 50. This psalm takes the form of a covenant lawsuit in which the Lord comes to confront his people in a formal manner (as in Isa 1:2-20). The Lord emphasizes that he places priority on obedience and genuine worship, not empty ritual.

Israel’s God is here identified with three names: El (אֵל [ʾel], or “God”), Elohim (אֱלֹהִים [ʾelohim], or “God”), and Yahweh (יְהוָה [yehvah] or “the Lord”). There is an obvious allusion here to Josh 22:22, the only other passage where these three names appear in succession. In that passage the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh declare, “El, God, the Lord! El, God, the Lord! He knows the truth! Israel must also know! If we have rebelled or disobeyed the Lord, don’t spare us today!” In that context the other tribes had accused the trans-Jordanian tribes of breaking God’s covenant by worshiping idols. The trans-Jordanian tribes appealed to “El, God, the Lord” as their witness that they were innocent of the charges brought against them. Ironically here in Ps 50 “El, God, the Lord” accuses his sinful covenant people of violating the covenant and warns that he will not spare them if they persist in their rebellion.

verses.zh: 从全美的锡安中，　神已经发光了。
verses.en: From Zion, the most beautiful of all places,[NOTE:1] God has come in splendor.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and calls [the] earth from the sunrise to its going.”
Heb “the perfection of beauty.”

verses.zh: 我们的　神要来，决不闭口。有烈火在他面前吞灭；有暴风在他四围大刮。
verses.en: “May our God comeand not be silent.”Consuming fire goes ahead of him,and all around him a storm rages.[NOTE:1]
notes: Has come in splendor. The psalmist may allude ironically to Deut 33:2, where God “shone forth” from Sinai.tn Or “shone forth.”

verses.zh: 他招呼上天下地，为要审判他的民，
verses.en: He summons the heavens above,as well as the earth, so that he might judge his people.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fire before him devours, and around him it is very stormy.”

verses.zh: 说：招聚我的圣民到我这里来，就是那些用祭物与我立约的人。
verses.en: He says:[NOTE:1] “Assemble my covenant people before me,[NOTE:2] those who ratified a covenant with me by sacrifice.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or perhaps “to testify against his people.”sn The personified heavens and earth (see v. 1 as well) are summoned to God’s courtroom as witnesses against God’s covenant people (see Isa 1:2). Long before this Moses warned the people that the heavens and earth would be watching their actions (see Deut 4:26; 30:19; 31:28; 32:1).
The words “he says” are supplied in the translation for clarification. God’s summons to the defendant follows.

Or “Gather to me my covenant people.” The Hebrew term חָסִיד (khasid, “covenant people”) elsewhere in the psalms is used in a positive sense of God’s loyal followers (see the note at Ps 4:3), but here, as the following line makes clear, the term has a neutral sense and simply refers to those who have outwardly sworn allegiance to God, not necessarily to those whose loyalty is genuine.

verses.zh: 诸天必表明他的公义，因为　神是施行审判的。（细拉）
verses.en: The heavens declare his fairness,[NOTE:1] for God is judge.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “the cutters of my covenant according to sacrifice.” A sacrifice accompanied the covenant-making ceremony and formally ratified the agreement (see Exod 24:3-8).
Or “justice.”

verses.zh: 我的民哪，你们当听我的话！以色列啊，我要劝戒你；我是　神，是你的　神！
verses.en: He says:[NOTE:1] “Listen, my people. I am speaking!Listen, Israel. I am accusing you.[NOTE:2] I am God, your God!
notes: Or “for God, he is about to judge.” The participle may be taken as substantival (as in the translation above) or as a predicate (indicating imminent future action in this context).
The words “he says” are supplied in the translation for clarification. God’s charges against his people follow.

verses.zh: 我并不因你的祭物责备你；你的燔祭常在我面前。
verses.en: I am not condemning[NOTE:1] you because of your sacrifices,or because of your burnt sacrifices that you continually offer me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Israel, and I will testify against you.” The imperative “listen” is understood in the second line by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Or “rebuking.”

verses.zh: 我不从你家中取公牛，也不从你圈内取山羊；
verses.en: I do not need to take[NOTE:1] a bull from your householdor goats from your sheepfolds.
notes: Heb “and your burnt sacrifices before me continually.”

verses.zh: 因为，树林中的百兽是我的，千山上的牲畜也是我的。
verses.en: For every wild animal in the forest belongs to me,as well as the cattle that graze on a thousand hills.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “I will not take.”

verses.zh: 山中的飞鸟，我都知道；野地的走兽也都属我。
verses.en: I keep track of[NOTE:1] every bird in the hills,and the insects[NOTE:2] of the field are mine.
notes: Heb “[the] animals on a thousand hills.” The words “that graze” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The term בְּהֵמוֹה (behemot, “animal”) refers here to cattle (see Ps 104:14).
Heb “I know.”

verses.zh: 我若是饥饿，我不用告诉你，因为世界和其中所充满的都是我的。
verses.en: Even if I were hungry, I would not tell you,for the world and all it contains belong to me.

verses.zh: 我岂吃公牛的肉呢？我岂喝山羊的血呢？
verses.en: Do I eat the flesh of bulls?Do I drink the blood of goats?[NOTE:1]
notes: The precise referent of the Hebrew word, which occurs only here and in Ps 80:13, is uncertain. Aramaic, Arabic and Akkadian cognates refer to insects, such as locusts or crickets.

verses.zh: 你们要以感谢为祭献与　神，又要向至高者还你的愿，
verses.en: Present to God a thank offering.Repay your vows to the Most High.[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical questions assume an emphatic negative response, “Of course not!”

verses.zh: 并要在患难之日求告我；我必搭救你，你也要荣耀我。
verses.en: Pray to me when you are in trouble.[NOTE:1] I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן, ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.
Heb “call [to] me in a day of trouble.”

verses.zh: 但　神对恶人说：你怎敢传说我的律例，口中提到我的约呢？
verses.en: God says this to the evildoer:[NOTE:1] “How can you declare my commands,and talk about my covenant?[NOTE:2]
notes: In vv. 7-15 the Lord makes it clear that he was not rebuking Israel because they had failed to offer sacrifices (v. 8a). On the contrary, they had been faithful in doing so (v. 8b). However, their understanding of the essence of their relationship with God was confused. Apparently they believed that he needed/desired such sacrifices and that offering them would ensure their prosperity. But the Lord owns all the animals of the world and did not need Israel’s meager sacrifices (vv. 9-13). Other aspects of the relationship were more important to the Lord. He desired Israel to be thankful for his blessings (v. 14a), to demonstrate gratitude for his intervention by repaying the vows they made to him (v. 14b), and to acknowledge their absolute dependence on him (v. 15a). Rather than viewing their sacrifices as somehow essential to God’s well-being, they needed to understand their dependence on him.

Heb “evil [one].” The singular adjective is used here in a representative sense; it refers to those within the larger covenant community who have blatantly violated the Lord’s commandments. In the psalms the “wicked” (רְשָׁעִים, reshaʿim) are typically proud, practical atheists (Ps 10:2, 4, 11) who hate God’s commands, commit sinful deeds, speak lies and slander, and cheat others (Ps 37:21).

verses.zh: 其实你恨恶管教，将我的言语丢在背后。
verses.en: For you hate instructionand reject my words.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “What to you to declare my commands and lift up my covenant upon your mouth?” The rhetorical question expresses sarcastic amazement. The Lord is shocked that such evildoers would give lip-service to his covenantal demands, for their lifestyle is completely opposed to his standards (see vv. 18-20).

verses.zh: 你见了盗贼就乐意与他同伙，又与行奸淫的人一同有分。
verses.en: When you see a thief, you join him;[NOTE:1] you associate with men who are unfaithful to their wives.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and throw my words behind you.”
Heb “you run with him.”

verses.zh: 你口任说恶言；你舌编造诡诈。
verses.en: You do damage with words,[NOTE:1] and use your tongue to deceive.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and with adulterers [is] your portion.”
Heb “your mouth you send with evil.”

verses.zh: 你坐着毁谤你的兄弟，谗毁你亲母的儿子。
verses.en: You plot against your brother;[NOTE:1] you slander your own brother.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and your tongue binds together [i.e., “frames”] deceit.”
Heb “you sit, against your brother you speak.” To “sit” and “speak” against someone implies plotting against that person (see Ps 119:23).

verses.zh: 你行了这些事，我还闭口不言，你想我恰和你一样；其实我要责备你，将这些事摆在你眼前。
verses.en: When you did these things, I was silent,[NOTE:1] so you thought I was exactly like you.[NOTE:2] But now I will condemn[NOTE:3] youand state my case against you.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “against the son of your mother you give a fault.”

The Lord was silent in the sense that he delayed punishment. Of course, God’s patience toward sinners eventually runs out. The divine “silence” is only temporary (see v. 3, where the psalmist, having described God’s arrival, observes that “he is not silent”).tn Heb “these things you did and I was silent.” Some interpret the second clause (“and I was silent”) as a rhetorical question expecting a negative answer, “[When you do these things], should I keep silent?” (cf. NEB). See GKC 335 §112.cc.

The Hebrew infinitive construct (הֱיוֹת, heyot) appears to function like the infinitive absolute here, adding emphasis to the following finite verbal form (אֶהְיֶה, ʾehyeh). See GKC 339-40 §113.a. Some prefer to emend הֱיוֹת (heyot) to the infinitive absolute form הָיוֹ (hayo).
Or “rebuke” (see v. 8).

verses.zh: 你们忘记　神的，要思想这事，免得我把你们撕碎，无人搭救。
verses.en: Carefully consider this, you who reject God.[NOTE:1] Otherwise I will rip you to shreds[NOTE:2] and no one will be able to rescue you.
notes: Heb “and I will set in order [my case against you] to your eyes.” The cohortative form expresses the Lord’s resolve to accuse and judge the wicked.
Heb “[you who] forget God.” “Forgetting God” here means forgetting about his commandments and not respecting his moral authority.

verses.zh: 凡以感谢献上为祭的便是荣耀我；那按正路而行的，我必使他得着我的救恩。
verses.en: Whoever presents a thank offering honors me.[NOTE:1] To whoever obeys my commands, I will reveal my power to deliver.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Elsewhere in the psalms this verb is used (within a metaphorical framework) of a lion tearing its prey (see Pss 7:2; 17:12; 22:13).
The reference to a thank-offering recalls the earlier statement made in v. 14. Gratitude characterizes genuine worship.
